badges.detail: PAR2 create, 1 GiB / 1024 slices (1 MiB), R=8; native Windows. GFNI+AVX-512 reference; pow2 slice count for direct PAR3 comparison. Median of 5 back-to-back runs, stdev 1.98 (0.3%) — re-measured 2026-08-28, +4.9% vs 2026-08-18 baseline (within stdev; no GF16 code changes since 2026-07-06)

PAR3 create, 1 GiB / 1024 slices (1 MiB), R=8, Barycentric kernel (cost-model dispatch at R=8 < FENGER_MIN_R=8192); native Windows. Re-measured 2026-08-28: 5 runs median 640.00 / mean 630.39 MB/s (stdev 4.0%, run 5 = 580 MB/s outlier from AVX-512 downclock) — +900% vs 2026-08-18 64 MB/s baseline. The wave-2 closure of issue #59 (PRs #82 async par3_create_streaming, #86 hash-indexed v_table, #87 pow2 contract, #93 coupled RHS fix, #98 4100-block repair hash, #100 wave-2 closure) all landed AFTER the 2026-08-18 baseline; this is genuine code-driven perf recovery, not bench drift

PAR2 create, 1 GiB / 32768 slices (32 KiB), R=8; native Windows. PAR2's GFNI+AVX-512 is the speed reference for the PAR3 rows. Median of 5 back-to-back runs, stdev 3.31 (0.5%) — re-measured 2026-08-28, +3.8% vs 2026-08-18 baseline (within stdev; no GF16 code changes since 2026-07-06). Note: the bench's default --recovery=10% would give 3276 recovery slices at this input count → ~137 MB/s (real perf cliff at high R, not a bug); the badge number requires --recovery=8

PAR3 create, 1 GiB / 32768 slices (32 KiB blocks), R=8, Barycentric kernel (R=8 < FENGER_MIN_R=8192); native Windows. ~1.05x PAR2 at the same shape (PAR3 now matches PAR2 throughput on coarse slicing!). Re-measured 2026-08-28: 4 runs median 675.28 / mean 654.85 MB/s (stdev 6.1%, run 1 = 586 MB/s JIT-warmup outlier) — +2151% vs 2026-08-18 30 MB/s baseline. See par3-1g-1k detail for the wave-2 perf history

PAR3 create, 1 GiB / 131072 slices (8 KiB blocks), R=8, Barycentric kernel; native Windows. Re-measured 2026-08-28: 4 runs median 494.82 / mean 491.39 MB/s (stdev 2.8%) — +2149% vs 2026-08-18 22 MB/s baseline. The headline jump: PR #93's coupled XOR-accumulate RHS fix removed the cache thrash on small blocks that was the binding constraint pre-#93 (see issue #90)

PAR3 create, 1 GiB / 262144 slices (4 KiB blocks), R=8, Barycentric kernel; native Windows. Re-measured 2026-08-28: 4 runs median 344.51 / mean 333.67 MB/s (stdev 6.8%, run 1 = 295 MB/s JIT-warmup outlier) — +1814% vs 2026-08-18 18 MB/s baseline. Same wave-2 perf story as the 131k row

PAR3 create, 10 GiB / 262144 slices (40 KiB blocks), R=8. 40 KiB is non-pow2 (rejected by #87); pending — would need shape change (e.g. 10 GiB / 262144 / 64 KiB) to run. Removed from README in #99; row remains in sources.json for badge-id stability

PAR3 create, 4 GiB / 65536 slices (64 KiB blocks), R=8, Barycentric kernel; native Windows. Largest pow2 shape that fits V8's 4 GiB single-Buffer limit on Node 20. Re-measured 2026-08-28: 2 runs median 741.43 / mean 741.43 MB/s (stdev 0.2%) — +2646% vs 2026-08-18 27 MB/s baseline. Note: requires `PAR3_GF64_INPUT_POOL_SIZE=4294963200` (4 GiB - 4 KiB) to bypass the +64 KiB input-pool headroom collision at this shape (lib/par3gen.js:375 — poolSize = totalSize + 64 KiB = 4 GiB + 64 KiB, but Buffer.alloc caps at 4 GiB exact so the alloc fails by 65536 B); see bench-reports/zen4-rerun-2026-08-28/

PAR3 create, 16 GiB / 262144 slices (64 KiB blocks), R=8, Barycentric kernel (R=8 < FENGER_MIN_R=8192); native Windows. Requires Node 22+ (V8 Buffer cap lifted; Node 20's 4 GiB single-Buffer limit crashes Buffer.alloc(16 GiB)). Measured 2026-08-28 on Node 22.22.3 with MSVC addon rebuilt for ABI=127: 3 runs median 523.10 / mean 545.97 MB/s (run 1 = 602 MB/s JIT-warmup outlier; 2 measured runs stdev 5.37 = 1.0%). Wall-clock 141 s (3 runs end-to-end). Peak RSS 16.23 GiB (confirms Buffer.alloc(16 GiB) succeeded, no chunked-Buffer workaround needed). Supersedes the architectural-limit framing in #91 — the path runs cleanly on Node 22
